title: E-Commerce Checkout
summary: Checkout turns a cart into a paid order without overselling stock or charging twice. The server reprices everything, holds inventory for a few minutes, lets the payment provider collect the card, and only creates the order when the provider confirms payment via webhook.

payment.label: Payment (card data never touches our servers)

walkthrough.title: Submit checkout
walkthrough.text: The storefront POSTs the cart ID and shipping address with an Idempotency-Key, so a double-click or network retry can't create two checkouts.

walkthrough.title: Reprice on the server
walkthrough.text: Prices, promotions, shipping, and tax are recomputed server-side. Totals sent by the client are never trusted.

walkthrough.title: Hold the stock
walkthrough.text: Inventory places a reservation with a TTL (e.g. 15 minutes). Stock is held, not yet decremented, so abandoned checkouts release it automatically.

walkthrough.title: Authorize payment
walkthrough.text: The checkout service creates a PaymentIntent and returns its client_secret. The browser confirms the card inside the provider's iframe, including any 3-D Secure challenge.

walkthrough.title: Webhook confirms
walkthrough.text: The provider calls the order service's webhook. The order is created idempotently, keyed on the PaymentIntent ID, and the reservation is committed.

walkthrough.title: Fulfil and notify
walkthrough.text: OrderPlaced is published through a transactional outbox to fulfilment and notifications. Payment is captured when the order ships.

data.label: Storefront Checkout UI
responsibilities: Collects address and contact details; displays server-computed totals, never its own.
Hosts the provider's card iframe so card numbers never reach our servers (keeps PCI scope minimal).
Disables the pay button and reuses one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt.

failureModes.scenario: User double-clicks Pay or the request is retried
failureModes.impact: Two checkouts and possibly two charges.
failureModes.mitigation: Idempotency-Key stored server-side; the same key returns the original result.

failureModes.scenario: Tab closed during the 3-D Secure challenge
failureModes.impact: Payment may succeed while the UI never sees the result.
failureModes.mitigation: Order creation is driven by the webhook, not the browser redirect; email confirms the order.

data.label: Checkout Orchestrator

output.name: To inventory
output.type: JSON: { checkoutId, items: [{ sku, qty }], ttl: 900 }

responsibilities: Runs checkout as a saga: reprice, reserve, authorize; each step has a compensating action (release hold, cancel intent).
Stores the idempotency key with the response, so retries replay the outcome instead of re-executing.
Applies per-step timeouts and gives the user a clear failure state rather than a spinner.

failureModes.scenario: Crash between reserving stock and creating the payment
failureModes.impact: Stock held for nobody; checkout stuck half-done.
failureModes.mitigation: Durable saga state; reservations expire via TTL even if compensation never runs.

failureModes.scenario: Price changed after the user saw the total
failureModes.impact: User is charged a different amount than shown.
failureModes.mitigation: Return a priceVersion; if the reprice differs, stop and show the new total for re-confirmation.

data.label: Cart, Pricing & Tax

input.name: Cart to price
input.type: JSON: { lines: [{ sku, qty }], address, promoCodes[] }

output.name: Priced cart
output.type: JSON: { lines[], discounts[], shipping, tax, total, currency, priceVersion }

responsibilities: Resolves current list prices and applies promotions in a defined, deterministic order.
Calculates shipping and destination-based tax for the shipping address.
Returns all amounts as integers in minor units (cents), so there are no floating-point rounding bugs.

failureModes.impact: Checkout blocks, or tax is wrong and becomes a liability.
failureModes.mitigation: Short timeout, then a cached rate table for the region, flagged for later reconciliation.

failureModes.impact: Negative or near-zero totals; coupon abuse spreads quickly.
failureModes.mitigation: Explicit stacking rules, a floor on total, and per-code usage limits enforced atomically.

data.label: Inventory Reservations

input.name: Reserve
input.type: JSON: { checkoutId, items: [{ sku, qty }], ttl }

responsibilities: Atomically checks available = onHand - reserved and records a hold, so two buyers can't get the last unit.
Expires holds after the TTL so abandoned carts return stock automatically.
Commits (decrements on-hand) only when the order is confirmed.

failureModes.impact: Row-lock contention makes every checkout slow or time out.
failureModes.mitigation: Split stock into sub-counters (bucketed rows) or an atomic Redis counter for hot SKUs.

failureModes.impact: Overselling: more units sold than exist.
failureModes.mitigation: Single conditional UPDATE … WHERE available >= qty, never a separate SELECT then UPDATE.

data.label: Payment Provider
responsibilities: Collects and tokenizes card data, runs 3-D Secure, and authorizes with the card network.
Holds funds (authorization) until capture, which is triggered at shipment.
Reports the final outcome via signed webhooks, retried until acknowledged.

failureModes.scenario: Webhook arrives twice or out of order
failureModes.impact: Duplicate orders or a 'failed' event overwriting a success.
failureModes.mitigation: Dedupe on event ID; fetch the latest intent status from the API instead of trusting event order.

failureModes.impact: Capture fails on a backordered item; goods shipped unpaid.
failureModes.mitigation: Re-authorize, or capture at order time for items that may ship late.

data.label: Order Service

output.name: OrderPlaced
output.type: Event: { orderId, items[], total, customer, shippingAddress }

responsibilities: Verifies the webhook signature, then creates the order with a unique constraint on paymentIntentId.
Writes the order and an OrderPlaced outbox row in one database transaction.
Commits the inventory reservation, and owns the order's lifecycle (placed, shipped, refunded).

failureModes.scenario: Order saved but event publish fails (dual write)
failureModes.impact: The customer is charged but the order never reaches the warehouse.
failureModes.mitigation: Transactional outbox: a relay publishes committed outbox rows, at least once.

failureModes.impact: Paid checkouts with no orders pile up.
failureModes.mitigation: The provider retries for days; a reconciler also lists recent succeeded intents with no order.

data.label: Fulfilment & Shipping

output.name: Shipment
output.type: Event: OrderShipped { orderId, carrier, trackingNumber } → triggers capture

responsibilities: Routes the order to a warehouse that has the stock, and generates pick lists and labels.
Emits OrderShipped, which triggers payment capture and the shipping email.
Handles partial shipments and backorders as separate shipments.

failureModes.mitigation: Idempotent consumer: a processed-event table keyed on event ID.

failureModes.impact: Orders queue up and delivery promises are missed.
failureModes.mitigation: Queue durably, alert on order age, re-route to an alternate warehouse.

data.label: Customer Notifications

output.name: Messages
output.type: Email / SMS: confirmation, tracking link, receipt

responsibilities: Sends the order confirmation and receipt, rendered from the order record rather than from the checkout session.
Sends shipping updates with tracking links.
Respects customer channel preferences and suppression lists.

failureModes.impact: Customers think the order failed and buy again.
failureModes.mitigation: Queue and retry; the order status page is the source of truth, not the email.
